items.headline: Singapore Cabinet reshuffle promotes five office-holders, effective 27 July
items.summary: A mid-term Cabinet reshuffle promotes five office-holders, with Tan See Leng becoming Minister for Trade and Industry (Energy and Industry), Ng Chee Meng returning to Cabinet as Minister in the PMO, and Jasmin Lau made Acting Minister for Manpower. K Shanmugam becomes Senior Minister while keeping Home Affairs and national-security coordination; changes take effect on 27 July.

items.headline: IRAS recovers S$6.8 million from eight nightclubs over flower-garland sales
items.summary: The Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore recovered about S$6.8 million in taxes and penalties from eight nightclubs that under-declared income from flower-garland sales, a customary tipping practice.

items.headline: No MRT delay over 30 minutes since November 2025, the best run since 2011: LTA
items.summary: The Land Transport Authority said Singapore's rail network has gone without a delay exceeding 30 minutes since November 2025, the longest such stretch since it began tracking the measure in 2011.

items.headline: S$230,000 Mercedes electric car catches fire at a Woodlands carpark
items.summary: A Mercedes-Benz electric vehicle bought less than three years ago for over S$230,000 caught fire at about 10am on 21 July near a multi-storey carpark at Block 548 Woodlands Drive 44. The blaze was extinguished and the cause is being investigated.

items.headline: Man who set fire to Joo Seng flat over neighbour delusions gets treatment order
items.summary: A 44-year-old man who started a fire at his Joo Seng flat while suffering delusions about a neighbour was given a mandatory treatment order instead of jail, with the court accepting his psychiatric condition contributed to the offence.

items.headline: Update: Rahul Gandhi freed after detention as MPs stage a Parliament 'Black Day'
items.summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi was released after being detained during the student-led 'Cockroach' protests over an alleged NEET exam-paper leak, and opposition MPs in black held a 'Black Day' demonstration inside Parliament on 22 July. The government offered a full discussion on the NEET row as the opposition demanded the education minister's resignation.

items.headline: Update: Sikkim tunnel blast toll rises to 20, with 13 bodies recovered
items.summary: The death toll from the 20 July gas blast that collapsed an under-construction tunnel at NHPC's 500MW Teesta Stage-VI hydro project in South Sikkim rose to at least 20, with 13 of 25 trapped workers' bodies recovered. Rescuers saw seven to eight more bodies but could not reach them as methane and waterlogging hampered the operation.

items.headline: India presses China on market access and the trade gap at ASEAN talks in Manila
items.summary: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar pressed Chinese counterpart Wang Yi for better market access, more predictable supply chains and steps to narrow a widening trade imbalance at a bilateral meeting on the sidelines of the ASEAN summit in Manila.

items.headline: India's largest asset manager makes a muted market debut after a $1 billion IPO
items.summary: Shares of India's biggest asset manager, the mutual-fund arm of State Bank of India, ended little changed on their first trading day after a roughly $1 billion IPO, a subdued debut amid weak market sentiment.

items.headline: UK inflation cools to a 15-month low as petrol and food prices ease
items.summary: UK consumer-price inflation fell more than forecast in June to its lowest in 15 months, helped by cheaper motor fuel and food, ahead of the Bank of England's next rate decision. Economists warned the reprieve could fade as the Middle East conflict lifts energy prices.

items.headline: Update: Conservatives urge HMRC to investigate Farage's GBP5 million gift
items.summary: The Conservative Party asked HM Revenue and Customs to examine whether Reform UK leader Nigel Farage owed tax on an undeclared GBP5 million gift from a donor, arguing it could count as 'disguised remuneration'. It adds a tax dimension to a standards inquiry and police probe already circling Reform's finances.

items.headline: Burnham stakes welfare reform on further education to cut youth unemployment
items.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham argued that expanding further education and training is central to curbing rising youth unemployment and welfare costs, though his team acknowledged the overhaul may raise spending in the short term.

items.headline: Burnham urges fiscal discipline at his first Cabinet meeting
items.summary: In his first Cabinet meeting, Andy Burnham pressed ministers to show fiscal discipline while repeating his pledge to ease the cost of living, saying the government was 'prepared to make difficult decisions' on the fiscal rules.

items.headline: Update: Trump vows to hit Iranian infrastructure for each Hormuz ship attack
items.summary: President Donald Trump threatened to bomb an Iranian bridge or power plant every time Tehran strikes vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, as the US launched fresh strikes on 22 July. Britain temporarily withdrew its diplomatic staff from Iran, and Trump attended the return of four US service members killed in the conflict at Dover.

items.headline: Ukraine's new military chief vows to intensify offensive operations on Russia
items.summary: Mykhailo Drapatyi, newly appointed by President Zelenskyy as Ukraine's top military commander, said the armed forces would 'continue and intensify offensive operations in all domains', including missions behind enemy lines.

items.headline: Ukrainian drones again strike warehouses of Russian retail giant Wildberries
items.summary: Ukrainian drones hit logistics centres belonging to Russia's largest online retailer, Wildberries, injuring eight people and forcing the evacuation of hubs in Krasnodar and Nevinnomyssk in a second such attack.

items.headline: Update: DR Congo Ebola outbreak nears 1,000 deaths, spreading faster than ever
items.summary: Nearly 1,000 people have died in DR Congo's Ebola outbreak - 999 confirmed deaths among about 2,473 cases since the Bundibugyo-strain outbreak began in May, the health ministry said. The WHO warns it is spreading faster than any previous outbreak, with no approved vaccine or treatment for the strain.

items.headline: Cybersecurity startup Glow leaves stealth at a $1.2 billion valuation
items.summary: Glow, founded by former Meta and Snowflake executives, emerged from stealth with a $180 million Series A led by Sequoia Capital, valuing it at $1.2 billion. Its platform uses AI agents to map enterprise devices and enforce security policies.

items.headline: An Anthropic-Physical Intelligence acquisition rumour sweeps AI circles
items.summary: A weekend rumour that Anthropic was acquiring robotics startup Physical Intelligence spread quickly before the startup's CEO denied it; the two held acquisition talks in the spring, per The Information. Physical Intelligence has raised over $1 billion and was recently in talks at an $11 billion valuation.

items.headline: Dimension Capital raises an $800 million fund for science-meets-compute startups
items.summary: Venture firm Dimension Capital closed an $800 million third fund, about 60% larger than its previous vehicle, backing startups at the intersection of the life sciences and computing.

items.headline: AMD launches Helios, its first rack-scale AI system, with Microsoft as a buyer
items.summary: AMD unveiled Helios, its first rack-scale AI system aimed at Nvidia, and said Microsoft will deploy the racks in Azure data centres, joining early customers Meta, OpenAI and Oracle. Helios ships later this year.

items.headline: Alphabet beats estimates as Google Cloud revenue jumps 82%
items.summary: Alphabet posted second-quarter revenue up 24% to $119.8 billion, beating forecasts, with Google Cloud accelerating 82% to $24.8 billion on AI demand. EPS came in at $9.11, and the company lifted planned 2026 capital spending to as much as $205 billion.

items.headline: Tesla profit weakens even as revenue climbs 26%; shares slide
items.summary: Tesla's second-quarter revenue rose about 26% to $28.24 billion, topping estimates, but GAAP net income was around $1.1 billion (roughly 32 cents a share) as gross margin slipped to 16.8% and operating margin to 1.4%. Operating expenses jumped 47% on AI and R&D spending and free cash flow was negative $1.1 billion; shares fell.

items.headline: IBM revenue disappoints as mainframe sales soften
items.summary: IBM reported second-quarter revenue of $17.2 billion, up just 1% and below the $17.58 billion expected, with adjusted EPS of $2.93 also short of estimates. CEO Arvind Krishna cited weaker Z mainframe and transaction-processing sales, and IBM trimmed 2026 revenue-growth guidance to 4%-5%.

items.headline: Wall Street dips as oil jumps ahead of a wave of Big Tech earnings
items.summary: US stocks slipped on 22 July, with the S&P 500 down about 0.1% and the Nasdaq 100 off 0.5%, as rising oil prices from the Iran conflict offset gains elsewhere before Alphabet and Tesla reported after the bell.

items.headline: 🏎️ Antonelli and Piastri among five drivers to sit out Hungarian GP first practice
items.summary: Championship leader Kimi Antonelli and McLaren's Oscar Piastri are among five drivers set to miss first practice at the Hungarian Grand Prix on 24 July, handing their cars to rookies under mandatory young-driver run-out rules. Antonelli's Mercedes goes to reserve Frederik Vesti, and he will not miss any further running.

items.headline: 🏎️ Aston Martin to debut its first big upgrade of 2026 at the Hungarian GP
items.summary: Aston Martin will introduce its first major car upgrade of the season at the Hungarian Grand Prix after a dismal start, with design chief Adrian Newey predicting 'a large step' from a reworked aero package that required rehomologating parts of the chassis. Fernando Alonso said he will decide his future during the summer break that follows the race.

items.headline: 🏏 Sooryavanshi stays confident as India open their Zimbabwe T20I series
items.summary: India begin a three-match T20I series in Harare on 23 July, with 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi - India's youngest international cricketer - saying he remains confident despite 'several ups and downs'. Captain Shreyas Iyer is under pressure after recent series defeats in Ireland and England.

items.headline: 🎾 Baez beats Kecmanovic in a battle of former champions at Kitzbuhel
items.summary: Sebastian Baez won an all-former-champions clash with Miomir Kecmanovic at the clay-court Generali Open in Kitzbuhel to advance to the next round.

items.headline: Astronomers spot the best candidate yet for a planet-sized 'exomoon'
items.summary: Using precise radial-velocity measurements, astronomers reported a planetary-mass 'exosatellite' - about 0.9 Jupiter masses - orbiting the brown-dwarf companion of the star CD-35 2722, the closest thing yet to a confirmed moon beyond our Solar System.

items.headline: A quantum computer learns to correct its own errors in real time
items.summary: Researchers combined reinforcement learning with quantum error correction so a quantum processor continuously recalibrates itself during a computation, reaching record-low logical error rates and resisting hardware drift, reported in Nature.

items.headline: The most complex sugar yet is detected in interstellar space
items.summary: Astronomers identified erythrulose, a four-carbon sugar, in a molecular cloud near the centre of the Milky Way - the most complex sugar found beyond the Solar System. Models suggest it forms on interstellar dust grains, hinting at how prebiotic sugars reached the early Earth.

items.headline: Scientists watch the ocean floor tear open and ooze lava in real time
items.summary: For the first time, instruments captured a seafloor-spreading event as it happened along the Southeast Indian Ridge, recording about 4 metres of subsidence and over 160 million cubic metres of lava erupting in roughly 16 days.

items.headline: Researchers describe a new monkey with orange lips and a frog-like roar
items.summary: Scientists have formally described a striking new monkey species notable for its orange lips and a deep, frog-like call, and warn the newly named primate may already be endangered.

fun_fact.headline: The Great Wall of China cannot be seen from space with the naked eye
fun_fact.body: Despite being one of the most repeated 'facts' about human-made structures, the Great Wall of China cannot be seen from space with the naked eye. Astronauts have confirmed it is invisible from low Earth orbit - the wall is only a few metres wide and blends into the surrounding land - and NASA has debunked the claim. Ironically, city lights, glasshouses and airport runways are far easier to pick out from orbit.

puzzle.title: Punch and Unfold
puzzle.body: A square sheet of paper is folded exactly in half from left to right, and then in half again from top to bottom, producing a smaller square four layers thick. A single hole is punched straight through all four layers, roughly in the middle of that folded square. When it is fully unfolded, how many holes are in the sheet, and how are they arranged relative to the centre?
puzzle.approach: Track how many layers the punch passes through, then use each fold crease as a mirror.
puzzle.answer: Four holes. Two folds double the thickness twice (1 -> 2 -> 4 layers), so a single punch pierces four layers. The fold creases are the sheet's vertical and horizontal centre-lines; unfolding mirrors the hole across each crease, leaving four holes arranged symmetrically - one per quadrant, all the same distance from the centre, forming a small rectangle around the middle.

word_puzzle.title: Cats and Dogs
word_puzzle.body: Turn CATS into DOGS in exactly three steps, changing one letter at a time; every intermediate rung must be a valid English word.
word_puzzle.approach: Change one letter at a time, keeping the other letters in place; every rung must be a real word.
word_puzzle.answer: CATS -> COTS -> COGS -> DOGS. CATS->COTS (a to o), COTS->COGS (t to g), COGS->DOGS (c to d). One letter changes on each rung and every step is a real word.
